Numerical Integration, Splitting, Stability, Scale Coupling, and Hybrid Events

Method-of-lines formulation and solver registry

Spatial discretization and operator assembly reduce deterministic RELIC processes to semi-discrete ordinary or differential-algebraic systems (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 25, 26, and 28):

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = f(t, x; \boldsymbol{\theta}) = f_J(t, x) + f_M(t, x) + f_G(t, x) + f_N(t, x), \qquad x(t_0) = x_0, \]

partitioning reversible (\(f_J\)), dissipative (\(f_M\)), boundary-port (\(f_G\)), and reaction (\(f_N\)) tendencies. relic.computation.solvers is the single solver owner (SolverBase, SolverRegistry, SolverFactory); scientific Functors never instantiate private solver registries.

Solver family

Status

Order and stability contract

RK4Solver (temporal.py)

Damped fixed-point implicit Euler

BackwardEulerSolver (temporal.py)

[I]

Order-1 implicit Euler solved by damped Picard iteration (\(\omega \in (0, 1]\), contraction limit \(\Delta t\,L_f < 1\) at \(\omega = 1\))

Symmetric midpoint & \(\vartheta\)-trapezoidal

ImplicitMidpointSolver, CrankNicolsonSolver (temporal.py), transactional_implicit_midpoint_step (geometric.py)

[I]

Order-2 symmetric midpoint and \(\vartheta\)-method (\(\vartheta = 0.5\) default) solved by fixed-point iteration (\(\frac{1}{2}\Delta t\,L_f < 1\) or \(\vartheta\Delta t\,L_f < 1\))

Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) Euler

IMEXEulerSolver (temporal.py)

[I]

Order-1 explicit non-stiff + damped fixed-point implicit stiff step (\(\Delta t\,L_{f_{\mathrm{imp}}} < 1\) at \(\omega = 1\))

ThomasAlgorithmSolver, solve_tridiagonal_thomas, solve_tridiagonal_batch (linear.py)

[I]

\(O(n)\) non-pivoting LU elimination with mandatory \(\lvert p_i \rvert \le \epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} s_i\) fail-fast guard and optional Varah condition estimate

BracketedBisectionSolver (nonlinear.py)

[I]

Guaranteed interval-halving root finder \(g(z^\ast) = 0\) with implicit-function autograd backward rule

Deterministic time-stepping, linear, and nonlinear solvers

Implemented one-step temporal integrators ([I])

RK4Solver advances smooth non-stiff systems on fixed float64 time grids via four stage evaluations:

\[ k_1 = f(t_n, x_n), \quad k_2 = f\!\left(t_n + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta t,\; x_n + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta t\,k_1\right), \quad k_3 = f\!\left(t_n + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta t,\; x_n + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta t\,k_2\right), \quad k_4 = f(t_n + \Delta t,\; x_n + \Delta t\,k_3), \]
\[ x_{n+1} = x_n + \frac{\Delta t}{6}\left(k_1 + 2k_2 + 2k_3 + k_4\right). \]

BackwardEulerSolver, ImplicitMidpointSolver, CrankNicolsonSolver (weight \(\vartheta = 0.5\) default), and IMEXEulerSolver (\(f = f_{\mathrm{exp}} + f_{\mathrm{imp}}\)) discretize:

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n + \Delta t\,f(t_{n+1}, x_{n+1}) \;\; (\text{Backward Euler}), \qquad x_{n+1} = x_n + \Delta t\,f\!\left(t_n + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta t,\; \tfrac{1}{2}(x_n + x_{n+1})\right) \;\; (\text{Implicit Midpoint}), \]
\[ x_{n+1} = x_n + \Delta t\left[(1 - \vartheta)f(t_n, x_n) + \vartheta f(t_{n+1}, x_{n+1})\right] \;\; (\text{Crank-Nicolson } \vartheta), \]
\[ x_{n+1} = x_n + \Delta t\,f_{\mathrm{exp}}(t_n, x_n) + \Delta t\,f_{\mathrm{imp}}(t_{n+1}, x_{n+1}) \;\; (\text{IMEX Euler}). \]

All four implicit solvers iterate fixed-point updates (damped Picard \(x^{(k+1)} = \omega G(x^{(k)}) + (1 - \omega)x^{(k)}\) with default damping_factor \(\omega = 1.0\) and max_iterations = 50 in Backward Euler and IMEX Euler; undamped fixed-point in Implicit Midpoint and Crank-Nicolson) without internal Newton-Raphson Jacobians. Consequently, A-stability of the underlying quadrature does not lift the Picard contraction restriction (\(\Delta t\,L_f < 1\), \(\frac{1}{2}\Delta t\,L_f < 1\), or \(\vartheta\Delta t\,L_f < 1\)). Finite non-convergent iterates return SolverStatus.MAX_ITERATIONS from solve() and raise SolverStepError in step() / forward(); non-finite iterates raise ValueError immediately. Standalone solvers perform fixed-grid stepping with no internal adaptive step resizing.

For discrete-gradient structure preservation on energy \(E\) and entropy \(S\) with \(\overline{\nabla}F(x_n, x_{n+1})^{\mathsf{T}}(x_{n+1} - x_n) = F(x_{n+1}) - F(x_n)\), skew \(J_h^{\mathsf{T}} = -J_h\) preserves energy \(E(x_{n+1}) - E(x_n) = \Delta t\,\overline{\nabla}E^{\mathsf{T}} J_h \overline{\nabla}E = 0\), and \(M_h \succeq 0\) guarantees discrete entropy production \(S(x_{n+1}) - S(x_n) = \Delta t\,\overline{\nabla}S^{\mathsf{T}} M_h \overline{\nabla}S \ge 0\) when functional, discrete gradient, and accepted step are explicitly bound.

Reference stiff solver families ([N])

Methods of Ecological Analysis (Chapters 25–26) derives four stiff Jacobian-based time-integration families as analytical benchmarks ([N] in relic.computation.solvers):

  1. Variable-order BDF (\(k = 1, \dots, 5\)): \(\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_j x_{n+1-j} = \Delta t\,\beta_0 f(t_{n+1}, x_{n+1})\), \(A(\alpha)\)-stable for stiff reaction-DAE kinetics;

  2. Linearly implicit Rosenbrock-W: \((I - \gamma \Delta t J_n) k_i = f(\dots) + \Delta t J_n \sum_{j < i} \gamma_{ij} k_j\) (\(J_n \approx \partial f / \partial x\)), avoiding nonlinear Newton loops via one linear solve per stage;

  3. High-order IMEX-ARK: paired explicit/diagonally-implicit Butcher tableaux \((\tilde{A}, \tilde{b}, \tilde{c})\) and \((A, b, c)\) treating advection/reactions explicitly and stiff vertical diffusion implicitly beyond order 1; and

  4. Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov (JFNK): inner GMRES/BiCGSTAB solves approximating directional derivatives \(J(x)v \approx [f(x + \varepsilon v) - f(x)]/\varepsilon\) for large coupled nonlinear residuals.

Tridiagonal linear and bracketed nonlinear solvers ([I])

1D vertical diffusion and linearized Richards discretizations assemble tridiagonal systems \(A x = d\) with lower, main, and upper diagonals \((a_i, b_i, c_i)\). ThomasAlgorithmSolver and solve_tridiagonal_thomas (relic.computation.solvers.linear) execute forward elimination and back substitution:

\[ p_i = b_i - a_i c_{i-1}' \;\; (p_0 = b_0), \qquad c_i' = \frac{c_i}{p_i}, \qquad d_i' = \frac{d_i - a_i d_{i-1}'}{p_i}, \qquad x_n = d_n', \quad x_i = d_i' - c_i' x_{i+1}. \]

Any non-finite pivot or near-zero pivot satisfying \(\lvert p_i \rvert \le \epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} s_i\) (where \(s_i\) is row \(i\)’s \(\ell_\infty\) norm) raises ValueError without pivot regularization. Enabling check_stability (computation.solvers.thomas.check_stability) records the Varah (1975) condition-number bound in SolverResult metadata.

BracketedBisectionSolver (relic.computation.solvers.nonlinear) solves scalar algebraic constraints \(g(z^\ast; \boldsymbol{\theta}) = 0\) on sign-change brackets \([a, b]\) (\(g(a)g(b) \le 0\)) and propagates exact implicit-function sensitivities through _ImplicitRootGradient:

\[ \frac{\partial z^\ast}{\partial \boldsymbol{\theta}} = -\left(\frac{\partial g(z^\ast, \boldsymbol{\theta})}{\partial z}\right)^{-1} \frac{\partial g(z^\ast, \boldsymbol{\theta})}{\partial \boldsymbol{\theta}}. \]

Multi-rate execution, operator splitting, and step control

Palindromic Strang splitting and SubFlowAccuracy

RELICSimulator partitions registered Functors into fast, medium, and slow groups (relic.core.simulator.execution_group, relic.core.simulator.execution_loop). For \(n \ge 2\) ordered fast-group processes \(F_1, \dots, F_n\), lie mode executes \(\Phi_n^{\Delta t} \circ \cdots \circ \Phi_1^{\Delta t}\), whereas strang mode executes the palindromic \(2n - 1\) composition (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 26):

\[ \Phi_{\Delta t}^{\mathrm{Strang}} = \Phi_1^{\Delta t / 2} \circ \cdots \circ \Phi_{n-1}^{\Delta t / 2} \circ \Phi_n^{\Delta t} \circ \Phi_{n-1}^{\Delta t / 2} \circ \cdots \circ \Phi_1^{\Delta t / 2}, \]

passing stage start time \(t\) to the leading half-steps and central full step and \(t + \Delta t / 2\) to the trailing half-steps. Each Functor declares FunctorMetadata.sub_flow_accuracy (SubFlowAccuracy in relic.core.functor.functor_types: EXACT with \(p_i = \infty\), ORDER_2 with \(p_i = 2\), ORDER_1 with \(p_i = 1\), or UNDECLARED), and RELICSimulator.get_splitting_order_report() evaluates the guaranteed one-step order:

\[\begin{split} q = \min\!\left(s,\; \min_{1 \le i \le n} p_i\right), \qquad s = \begin{cases} 1, & \texttt{lie}, \\ 2, & \texttt{strang}, \end{cases} \end{split}\]

reporting unverified whenever any participating process leaves SubFlowAccuracy.UNDECLARED. Strang composition with first-order explicit Euler sub-integrators reduces globally to \(q = 1\). In Strang mode with \(n \ge 2\), State Contract Model (SCM) flux edges between stateful fast members (including stateless relays) are refused at provider publication; IntegrationPlan (relic.computation.solvers.geometric) validates static stage DAGs as metadata_only (verified=False, runtime_ready=False), while runtime schedule conformance is verified via RELICSimulator.get_composition_plan() and GraphExecutor.integration_plan_witness.

Multi-rate effective interval and boundary-rate integrals

With base fast step \(\Delta t_f\), the medium group triggers across multiples of medium_interval_seconds, and the slow group triggers across multiples of slow_interval_seconds (or calendar month boundaries when unset), receiving the exact elapsed interval since its prior execution:

\[ \Delta t_{\mathrm{eff}} = t_{\mathrm{future}} - t_{\mathrm{last}}, \qquad \Delta t_{\mathrm{eff}} > 0. \]

Each group execution (and each Strang sub-execution) commits immediately through StateManager. Across substeps \(k\) of duration \(h_k\) within call interval \(H = \sum_k h_k\), ACCUMULATE amounts sum directly, ACCUMULATE rates (per_timestep=False) form time-weighted averages \(\sum_k (h_k / H) q_k\), and substepped physical boundary-port REPLACE rates (allowed_in / allowed_out) commit the exact interval mean \(\sum_k q_k \Delta t_k / \Delta t_{\mathrm{call}}\). Declared multirate_exchanges supply either hold or piecewise-constant running interval_mean overlays (exchange_mean__<id>) to slower consumers.

RMS update-magnitude step controller

RELICSimulator.run(...) adapts macro-steps exclusively via the fast-group committed root-mean-square (RMS) update metric over the \(m\) distinct state variables written by the fast group (\(u_k = x'_k - x_k\)):

\[ \tau_k = \mathrm{atol} + \mathrm{rtol}\,\lvert x_k \rvert, \qquad \mathrm{Err} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{m}\sum_{k=1}^{m} \operatorname{mean}\!\left(\frac{u_k}{\tau_k}\right)^2}. \]

If \(\mathrm{Err} > 1\) and \(\Delta t > \Delta t_{\min}\), the step rolls back and retries once with \(\Delta t_{\mathrm{new}} = \max\!\left(\Delta t_{\min},\; \Delta t\max(0.1, 0.9 / \sqrt{\mathrm{Err}})\right)\); accepted steps propose \(\Delta t_{\mathrm{next}} = \operatorname{clip}\!\left(\Delta t\min(5, \max(0.1, 0.9 / \sqrt{\mathrm{Err}})),\; \Delta t_{\min},\; \Delta t_{\max}\right)\) (doubling when \(\mathrm{Err} = 0\)). This controller bounds relative state jumps and is distinct from formal embedded truncation-error or Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability control.

Transport stability and nonlinear Richards closure

For 1D/multi-D advection-diffusion \(\frac{\partial c}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot(\mathbf{u}c - D\nabla c) = 0\) on isotropic grid spacing \(\Delta x\) in \(d\) spatial dimensions, explicit time stepping is constrained by the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) number, explicit Fourier diffusion number \(\mu\), and cell Peclet number \(\mathrm{Pe}\) (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 25):

\[ \mathrm{CFL} = \frac{\lvert u \rvert\,\Delta t}{\Delta x} \le C_{\max}, \qquad \mu = \frac{D\,\Delta t}{\Delta x^2} \le \frac{1}{2d}, \qquad \mathrm{Pe} = \frac{\lvert u \rvert\,\Delta x}{D}. \]

apply_advection (relic.scientific.transport) enforces \(\mathrm{CFL} \le C_{\max}\) against transport.numerical.cfl_advection_max (default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.0]) on explicit "euler" steps and raises ValueError on violation (upwind supports all integrators; lax_wendroff, superbee, and van_leer require "euler"; central requires "implicit_midpoint" or "crank_nicolson").

Variably saturated vertical soil-water flow obeys the mixed-form Richards equation with van Genuchten (1980) retention and Mualem (1976) hydraulic conductivity:

\[ \frac{\partial \theta(h)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left[K(h)\left(\frac{\partial h}{\partial z} + 1\right)\right] - S(h), \qquad S_e = \left[1 + (\alpha \lvert h \rvert)^n\right]^{-m} \;\; \left(m = 1 - \frac{1}{n}\right), \]
\[ \theta(h) = \theta_r + S_e(\theta_s - \theta_r), \qquad K(S_e) = K_s S_e^\ell\left[1 - \left(1 - S_e^{1/m}\right)^m\right]^2, \]

routing any saturation or residual-moisture clipping (\(\theta_r \le \theta \le \theta_s\)) into explicit water-budget ledgers.

Conservative spatial remapping and internal cross-domain couplers

Basis-governed spatial remapping

Grid-to-grid (ConservativeRemap, ConservativeRegridder, BilinearRegridder, NearestNeighborRegridder in relic.coupling.scales.spatial) and nested-unit hierarchical operators (HierarchicalAggregator, ScaleManager in relic.coupling.scales) enforce SpatialQuantityBasis (relic.coupling.scales.types: intensive, cell_total, area_density, categorical; see Mathematical Foundations). Spherical latlon cell areas use SSOT earth_radius \(R_\oplus\) as \(A = R_\oplus^2(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)(\sin\phi_2 - \sin\phi_1)\), and HierarchicalAggregator additionally supports neutral-drag effective roughness blending at reference height \(z_r\) (\(0 < z_{0,i} < z_r\)):

\[ z_{0,j} = z_r \exp\!\left[-\left(\sum_i \frac{f_{ij}}{\ln^2(z_r / z_{0,i})}\right)^{-1/2}\right]. \]

Internal cross-domain coupling ports (relic.coupling.internal)

Three ScaleCouplingFunctor ports connect soil, vegetation, and surface-layer variables without duplicating domain process laws (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 23–24):

  1. SoilVegetationCoupling (relic.coupling.internal.soil_vegetation): Normalizes parametric (exponential, linear, beta) or observed root density across layer thicknesses \(\Delta z_i\) (\(\sum_i \beta_i \Delta z_i = 1\)) and applies the four-threshold Feddes matric-potential stress factor \(\alpha(\psi_i) \in [0, 1]\) (\(\psi_{\mathrm{wilt}} < \psi_{\mathrm{opt,dry}} < \psi_{\mathrm{opt,wet}} < \psi_{\mathrm{anaer}}\)) to potential transpiration \(T_p\):

\[ S_i = \alpha(\psi_i)\,\beta_i\,T_p, \qquad T_{\mathrm{actual}} = \sum_i S_i\,\Delta z_i \le T_p. \]

  1. BiosphereAtmosphereCoupling (relic.coupling.internal.biosphere_atmosphere): Maps friction velocity \(u_\ast > 0\), air temperature \(T > 0\), and pressure \(P > 0\) to bulk-canopy leaf boundary-layer conductance:

\[ g_{b,\mathrm{ms}} = C_v\sqrt{\frac{u_\ast}{d_{\mathrm{leaf}}}}, \qquad g_{b,\mathrm{mol}} = g_{b,\mathrm{ms}}\frac{P}{R T}. \]

  1. WaterCarbonCoupling (relic.coupling.internal.water_carbon): Combines soil-moisture factor \(f_{\mathrm{soil}}(\theta)\) (logistic, linear, or piecewise), hyperbolic vapour-pressure-deficit factor \(f_{\mathrm{vpd}} = (1 + D / D_{50})^{-1}\), and clamped \(Q_{10}\) thermal response \(f_T\) into bounded physiological and decomposition modifiers (\(f_{\mathrm{gpp}}\), \(f_{Ra}\), \(f_{Rh}\), \(k_{\mathrm{dec}}\), and \(f_{\mathrm{overall}}\)).

Transverse hybrid events and saltation-matrix sensitivities

For one transversal zero crossing of a scalar guard \(g(x, \boldsymbol{\theta}, t) = 0\) within an explicit step \([t_0, t_0 + \Delta t]\) (\(g_0 g_1 \le 0\)) followed by a smooth reset map \(x^+ = R(x^-, \boldsymbol{\theta}, \tau)\), relic.computation.solvers.hybrid_events (locate_guard_crossing, event_time_sensitivity, sensitivity_jump, saltation_matrix) locates the crossing time \(\tau\) by linear interpolation and propagates exact first-order state and parameter sensitivities (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 28):

\[ \tau = t_0 + \Delta t\,\frac{g_0}{g_0 - g_1}, \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}\tau}{\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\theta}} = -\frac{g_x S^- + g_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}{g_x f^- + g_t}, \]
\[ \Xi = R_x + \frac{\left(f^+ - R_x f^- - R_t\right) n^{\mathsf{T}}}{n^{\mathsf{T}} f^- + g_t} \quad \left(n = g_x^{\mathsf{T}}\right), \qquad S^+ = R_x S^- + R_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} + \left(R_x f^- + R_t - f^+\right)\frac{\mathrm{d}\tau}{\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\theta}}, \]

where \(f^-\) and \(f^+\) are pre- and post-event vector fields and \(S^-\), \(S^+\) are pre- and post-event parameter sensitivities. Tangential or grazing trajectories satisfying \(\lvert g_0 - g_1 \rvert \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{trans}}\) or \(\lvert n^{\mathsf{T}} f^- + g_t \rvert \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{trans}}\) (computation.solvers.hybrid_events.transversality_tolerance, default 1e-12) raise ValueError without extrapolation. Production consumer: GDDPhenology onset diagnostics; simultaneous multi-guard crossings and implicit-solver event location remain [N].

Stochastic, memory, ALE, DAE, and topology-transition families

relic.stochastic provides standalone Ito Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) Euler-Maruyama stepping (\(x_{n+1} = x_n + a(x_n, t_n)\Delta t + B(x_n, t_n)\Delta W_n\), \(\Delta W_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Delta t\,I)\), strong order \(1/2\)), Gillespie direct Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA) reaction jumps (\(\tau = -\ln u_1 / a_0(x)\), \(x^+ = x^- + \nu_j\)), and Monte Carlo ensemble statistics (\(\bar{x} = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M x^{(m)}\), \(s_x^2 = \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{m=1}^M (x^{(m)} - \bar{x})^2\)). Conservative stochastic forcing acts on flux cochains (\(\mathrm{d}x_{\mathrm{noise}} = -D_{d-1,h}\Xi_h\,\mathrm{d}W_t\)) so closed elemental ledgers remain invariant.

Across the certified scientific Functors, six bounded non-standard dynamical families are wired into FunctorBase, StateManager, and checkpoint/restart governance ([I]):

Semantic family

Governed production Functor(s)

Mathematical realization and scope boundary

continuous_sde

OrnsteinUhlenbeckTemperatureFunctor (Level 2)

Euler-Maruyama Ornstein-Uhlenbeck anomaly step with deterministic per-Functor substream checkpoint/restart replay (FunctorSubstreamMixin)

marked_jump

MarkedPoissonRainfallFunctor (Level 2)

Constant-hazard Poisson storm arrivals with exponential depth marks and deterministic substream replay; steps exceeding arrival cap fail closed without truncation

memory

TwoRegionMassTransferFunctor (Level 3)

Exact exponential integrating-factor realization (SubFlowAccuracy.EXACT) of mobile-immobile Volterra memory exchange \(f_{\mathrm{mem}}(t) = -\int_0^t K(t-s)e(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\)

ale

MovingDomainDiffusionFunctor (Level 3)

1D Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) uniform column stretching satisfying the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL) and moving-metric power identity \(e_E^{\mathsf{T}} f_{\mathrm{ALE}} = -\frac{1}{2}x^{\mathsf{T}}\dot{\star}_h x\)

descriptor_dae

EquilibriumSorptionFunctor (Level 2)

Total-mass prognostic advance paired with index-1 Freundlich Differential-Algebraic Equation (DAE) scalar root solve via BracketedBisectionSolver

topology_change

HortonianPondingEventFunctor & SurfacePondingFunctor (Level 2)

Guard-triggered ponding topology registration with affine state remap, water-budget closure, and single provider-epoch transition
